title: Security Review and Best Practices knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Security Review and Best Practices”?
options: Security Review and Best Practices means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Security Review and Best Practices removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Security Review and Best Practices should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Security Review and Best Practices helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Security Review and Best Practices helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Security Review and Best Practices is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Threat modeling” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Threat modeling” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Threat modeling” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Threat modeling” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Threat modeling” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Threat modeling” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Threat modeling” under Security Review and Best Practices. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Security Review and Best Practices”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
